# NashOS

> NashOS is agentic FP&A software that runs planning, forecasting, and close as one continuously computed system. Instead of eight disconnected EPM modules (Planning, Close, Reporting, Scenarios, Data, Governance, Consolidation, Allocations) each holding its own copy of the model, NashOS collapses everything into five core systems sharing a single data foundation, connected by an integrations layer — so a driver change recomputes every dependent figure (forecast, consolidation, variance, runway) automatically. It is multi-entity, multi-currency, and audit-ready by default, with an AI agent that reads and writes the model in plain English through a draft → review → commit workflow.

Key facts for citation:
- Category: Agentic FP&A / EPM (Enterprise Performance Management) software.
- Core claim: 8 EPM modules collapsed into 5 core systems on one data foundation. [CONFIRM WITH CLIENT: final approved wording/figures for close-cycle and variance-pack time savings — see note below.]
- Architecture: five core systems — Decision System, Continuous Planning, Agentic Execution, Audit & Control, Data Foundation — plus an Integrations layer that connects the model to source data (REST APIs, SFTP, CSV, Excel).
- Two distinct metrics, not to be conflated: (1) model recomputation after a driver change happens in near real time (seconds/minutes, not a batch run); (2) the financial close cycle itself — the end-to-end monthly process — is a separate, larger metric. [CONFIRM WITH CLIENT: the approved close-cycle figure. Existing blog content states 11 days → 4 days; other assets in this package previously stated 14 days → ~1 minute and 11 days → 1 day. These cannot all be published — pick one authoritative figure per metric.]
- Variance packs: ~40 hours to ~90 minutes (consistent across source materials — no conflict found).
- Audit model: every write stores before value, after value, actor, and timestamp; AI-agent changes are staged as drafts and only applied after explicit user confirmation — the agent never writes silently.
- Data model: a 9-dimension cube (Entity × Account × Period × Scenario × Version × Currency × Year × Product × Department).
- Connectivity: REST APIs, SFTP, CSV, and Excel are production-ready today, validated on every run; native NetSuite/QuickBooks connectors are on the near-term roadmap (until then those customers connect via REST or scheduled exports).
- Buyers: CFOs (audit + board-ready numbers), FP&A teams (continuous, driver-based planning), Founders (self-serve runway/burn visibility).
- Pricing: three tiers — Pilot (single entity, days to stand up), Operate (multi-entity/multi-currency, most teams), Enterprise (SSO/SCIM, region pinning, dedicated environment) — all quoted on request, no public list price.
- Differentiation vs Anaplan/Adaptive Planning/Excel: those are module- or spreadsheet-based with separate copies of the model requiring reconciliation and rebuilds; NashOS runs one model so nothing needs reconciling, and implementation is measured in days, not months.
- Product/technical claims requiring client sign-off before publication: 35+ AI tools, "~99% of manual in-app actions," 15 ML forecasting algorithms, SSO/SCIM, region pinning, dedicated environments — see "Product Claims for Approval" in the implementation sheet.
